tweet.text:
I saw a vision today, barefoot in our front lawn, blowing bubbles with my little girl. She was a whirlwind of joy, chasing those soapy spheres with all the breath her tiny lungs could muster. She was thrashing after each bubble like it was the last one in the universe.

I got to thinking about it all—time, space, the whole shebang. Each bubble, you see, was like a universe to me. They'd pop into existence, have their brief moment in the sun, and then—poof—gone. In that flash of time, I fancied they had whole lives, trillions of souls living out their dramas, just like us. 

There I was, rooting for these fragile universes against my own child's innocent onslaught. I hoped for their survival, their persistence. In each bubble, I saw myself, just a speck, fretting over the rent, the mundane worries of existence. But in that moment, I was rooting for the cosmos, for everything.

Then I stepped back, looked up at the blue sky, and I thought, I really hoped, that somewhere out there, someone was rooting for me, too.
